idiom_name: struct of function pointers backed by an in-memory table
implementation_notes: C has no interfaces, so the fake is hand-built: the collaborator's role becomes a struct of function pointers, and the fake is an implementation of that table whose callbacks read and write an in-memory store. The module under test must receive the table (a context or handle parameter) instead of calling the real functions directly, so the substitutable dependency is explicit. Nothing in C replaces the classic structure - code generators such as CMock produce mocks with queued expectations, not working fakes - so hand-writing the in-memory implementation remains the only route.
pitfalls: File-scope state (static arrays and counters) makes the fake shared by every test in the binary: reset it in setup, or let the fake own a store struct that the test allocates per case.
Function-pointer members are plain copies and their parameter lists are not checked across translation units, so a signature drift compiles and fails at runtime - unlike a C++ override.
A fake that ignores the module's error convention (return codes, errno) silently changes the code under test's error paths.
